layers.name: Governance Kernel
layers.description: The governed-work core: plugin manifest plus the README catalog that declares all 32 Work Instructions and their IDs. This is the contract layer — it defines what the plugin is, who owns it, and which skills must exist.

layers.name: Construction Trade Skills (CSI Divisions)
layers.description: Trade-specific Work Instruction skills keyed to CSI MasterFormat divisions: concrete (Div 03), structural steel (Div 05), plumbing (Div 22), HVAC (Div 23), and electrical (Div 26). These are the physical-construction skills — what gets built and how. Maps to the PM/Super/Estimating execution surface.

layers.name: Safety & Quality Control Skills
layers.description: Sage CM Work Instructions covering safety, quality, and inspection workflows: morning huddles/toolbox talks, safety equipment checks, hold-point inspections, QC audits, regulator/AHJ inspections, and compliance audits/notices. This is the construction-safety + construction-quality control surface.

layers.name: Cost, Scheduling & Field Operations
layers.description: Sage CM Work Instructions that drive daily operations, scheduling, cost/logistics, and field monitoring: 3-Week Look Ahead, Daily Log Entry, Field Monitoring, Material Receiving, Go Codes equipment scans, Housekeeping, Photo Documentation, and RFI processing. Maps to construction-cost + construction-scheduling + construction-super operations.

layers.name: Closeout & Project Records
layers.description: End-of-job Work Instructions: Punchlist Closeout and As-Built Updates. These finalize the project, freeze records, and feed the construction-closeout surface.

layers.name: Doctrine & UA-Treatment Reference
layers.description: Non-runtime documentation and Understand-Anything treatment outputs: the wiki entity/concept pages, schema, index; the explain/onboard markdown guides; the dashboard, knowledge-graph, domain-flow, chat-response, diff-analysis, and receipt manifests. Doctrine + reference material that explains the surface without being part of it.

tour.title: Start at the Governance Kernel — what the plugin promises
tour.narrative: The README is the catalog of contracts. It declares all 32 Work Instructions (Atlas STDWORK SOP WI Wiring V1) and maps every WI ID to a title. The plugin.json manifest registers tcs-construction v1.0.0 with Claude Code under SSU Fleet. Everything downstream in the tour exists because the README named it — this is the governed-work kernel for the construction surface.
tour.why: You cannot evaluate or extend any skill until you know which skills the plugin claims to own. Start at the contract.

tour.title: Drop into Construction PM — CSI-division trade skills
tour.narrative: Each trade skill (Structural Steel d05, Concrete Slab Rebar d03, Plumbing d22, HVAC d23, Electrical d26) follows the same SKILL.md shape: trigger, prerequisites, steps, outputs, Jr coaching notes, and quality gates. This is the PM/Super execution surface — the physical-construction work that has to happen on site.
tour.why: These skills define WHAT is built. They are the anchors that every safety, quality, cost, and closeout skill orbits around.

tour.title: Wrap trade work in Safety — morning huddle and SE check
tour.narrative: Before any d0X trade skill fires in the field, the Morning Huddle / Toolbox Talk runs the crew through hazards and the daily plan. Safety Equipment Check verifies PPE and gear. Post-Rain SWPPP Inspection handles environmental compliance after weather events. These are the daily safety gates that gate access to the trade skills.
tour.why: Construction safety is enforced as a hard prerequisite, not an afterthought. The huddle starts the day; the gear check enforces it.

tour.title: Then Quality Control — hold points, QC audits, AHJ inspections
tour.narrative: Hold Point Inspection blocks trade work until quality is verified at a defined milestone (e.g., rebar before pour, rough-in before close-up). QC Audit walks the spec compliance. Regulator/AHJ Inspection coordinates the outside authority. Compliance Audit + Comply Notice handle program-level compliance. Together these form the construction-quality control loop that pairs with each trade skill in Layer 2.
tour.why: Quality control is where TCS turns from a checklist into a governed system — hold points are explicit pauses where work cannot proceed without sign-off.

tour.title: Cost and Scheduling — 3WLA + Daily Log keep the project on rails
tour.narrative: The 3-Week Look Ahead is the forward-looking schedule artifact: what's coming in the next 21 days. The Daily Log is the backward-looking record: what actually happened today (the 'Silence is Failure' principle). Field Monitoring keeps eyes on production. RFI Processing handles design questions that block work. Together these are the cost+schedule heartbeat.
tour.why: Schedule is set in the 3WLA and confirmed in the Daily Log. Without both, the surface has no idea whether the trade work is on track.

tour.title: Logistics and field evidence — material receiving, Go Codes, photo doc
tour.narrative: Material Receiving confirms that ordered material arrived and matches the PO. Go Codes Equipment Scan tracks equipment in/out via QR. Housekeeping enforces site condition standards. Photo Documentation creates the visual evidence trail that backs the Daily Log and the eventual closeout package. These are the supporting field-ops skills that wrap the schedule.
tour.why: Construction is a logistics problem. These skills produce the evidence that downstream cost reconciliation and closeout will depend on.

tour.title: Closeout — punchlist and as-built finalize the project record
tour.narrative: When substantial completion approaches, Punchlist Closeout drives the final defect list to zero. As-Built Updates capture every field deviation back into the drawing set so the owner inherits a true record. These are the construction-closeout endpoints — once they fire successfully, the project is governable as a finished record.
tour.why: A project is not done until its records are honest. Closeout skills are where the governed-work kernel pays off as a turnover-ready archive.

tour.title: Cross-cutting reference — UA-treatment doctrine and wiki
tour.narrative: The Understand-Anything treatment outputs (onboard guide, explainer, knowledge graph, dashboard, wiki pages, and the receipt manifest) sit alongside the skills as reference doctrine. They are how new operators decode the plugin — not part of the runtime surface, but the cross-cutting documentation layer that explains it. Start here on day one; come back here when teaching.
tour.why: Skills execute. Doctrine explains. Both ship together so the next operator has a path in.
